meta.provenance: Authored from model knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026). Original explanations. Component names/tabs are factual data.
meta.iconNote: App uses its Grasshopper sprite sheet (see globals.css) or chip fallback.

commands.name: Point
commands.description: A container parameter that holds one or more points, either referenced from Rhino or inherited from upstream components. Use it to pin point data in place, internalise it, or keep a definition tidy.

commands.name: Curve
commands.description: A container parameter for curve geometry referenced from Rhino or passed along a wire. Handy for staging referenced curves at the start of a definition and for internalising geometry so the file is self-contained.

commands.name: Surface
commands.description: A container parameter for untrimmed or trimmed surfaces. Reference surfaces from the Rhino model or store intermediate results so later parts of the graph read clearly.

commands.name: Brep
commands.description: A container parameter for boundary-representation solids and polysurfaces. Use it to reference Rhino polysurfaces into the canvas or to hold the output of solid operations.

commands.name: Mesh
commands.description: A container parameter for mesh geometry. Reference Rhino meshes or store meshes generated on the canvas before analysis or export.

commands.name: Geometry
commands.description: A general-purpose container that accepts any geometry type — points, curves, surfaces, breps or meshes. Useful when a definition must handle mixed input without caring what kind it is.

commands.name: Geometry Pipeline
commands.description: Streams Rhino objects onto the canvas automatically by filtering on layer name, object name and type. Because it updates live as the model changes, it suits workflows where Rhino remains the master model.

commands.name: Number
commands.description: A container for floating-point numbers. Use it to label numeric wires, set persistent values or collect results from calculations.

commands.name: Integer
commands.description: A container for whole numbers. It rounds incoming values to integers, which makes it useful ahead of components that count items or index into lists.

commands.name: Boolean
commands.description: A container for true/false values. Use it to store logical states that drive components such as Dispatch or Cull Pattern.

commands.name: Text
commands.description: A container for text strings. Useful for labels, file paths and any wire that carries words rather than numbers.

commands.name: Domain
commands.description: A container for one-dimensional numeric domains (an interval between two values). Domains describe curve and surface parameter spaces, so this parameter often sits beside Range or Remap Numbers.

commands.name: Colour
commands.description: A container for ARGB colour values. Feed it into Custom Preview or Gradient workflows to control how geometry is displayed.

commands.name: Data
commands.description: A generic container that accepts any data type without conversion. Use it as a neutral relay to tidy long wires or to internalise mixed data.

commands.name: Number Slider
commands.description: An interactive slider that outputs a number within a user-defined range and precision. It is the primary way to drive a parametric model by hand, so almost every definition starts with one.

commands.name: Panel
commands.description: A multi-purpose text panel that displays whatever data is wired into it, or supplies typed text and numbers when used as an input. It is the standard tool for inspecting lists and data trees while you work.

commands.name: Value List
commands.description: A drop-down (or cycle/check-list) of named values you define, outputting the item the user picks. Use it to offer a controlled set of options, such as preset dimensions or mode switches.

commands.name: Boolean Toggle
commands.description: A simple switch that outputs True or False when double-clicked. Typical uses include turning previews on and off and switching between two branches of a definition.

commands.name: Button
commands.description: A momentary push button that outputs True only while pressed, then reverts to False. Use it to fire one-off actions such as baking geometry or resetting a solver.

commands.name: MD Slider
commands.description: A two-dimensional slider that outputs a point in the unit square, effectively two coupled values at once. It is convenient for picking UV coordinates on a surface interactively.

commands.name: Graph Mapper
commands.description: Remaps a stream of numbers through an editable graph curve such as linear, bezier, sine or parabola. Use it to shape distributions — for example easing the spacing of floor heights or attractor falloff.

commands.name: Gradient
commands.description: Converts numbers within a domain into colours sampled along an editable colour ramp. It is the standard bridge between analysis results and coloured previews.

commands.name: Colour Swatch
commands.description: Outputs a single colour chosen from a picker. Wire it into Custom Preview to give geometry a fixed display colour.

commands.name: Expression
commands.description: Evaluates a written formula over one or more input variables, supporting arithmetic, conditionals and a library of functions. Use it to collapse several operator components into a single legible expression.

commands.name: Addition
commands.description: Adds two values and outputs the result; it also concatenates where the data type supports it. One of the basic operator components used throughout numeric workflows.

commands.name: Subtraction
commands.description: Subtracts the second input from the first. Use it for offsets between values, differences of coordinates or countdowns in sequences.

commands.name: Multiplication
commands.description: Multiplies two values together. Commonly used to scale numeric lists, apply factors to distances, or combine sliders.

commands.name: Division
commands.description: Divides the first input by the second. Useful for ratios, normalising values and converting totals into per-unit quantities.

commands.name: Modulus
commands.description: Returns the remainder after dividing the first input by the second. A staple for cyclic patterns, such as alternating every nth item in a facade grid.

commands.name: Mass Addition
commands.description: Sums an entire list into a single total and also outputs the running (partial) sums. The partial results are especially useful for cumulative dimensions such as stacked floor levels.

commands.name: Equality
commands.description: Compares two values and outputs True where they are equal and False where they differ. Combine it with Cull Pattern or Dispatch to filter data by matching values.

commands.name: Larger Than
commands.description: Tests whether the first value is greater than the second, outputting a Boolean for each pair. Use it to threshold analysis results before filtering geometry.

commands.name: Smaller Than
commands.description: Tests whether the first value is less than the second, outputting True or False per item. Often paired with Dispatch to split a list around a threshold.

commands.name: Gate And
commands.description: Returns True only when both Boolean inputs are True. Use it to combine several conditions into one filter pattern.

commands.name: Gate Or
commands.description: Returns True when at least one of the two Boolean inputs is True. Useful for merging alternative pass conditions before culling or dispatching.

commands.name: Construct Domain
commands.description: Builds a numeric domain from a start and end value. Domains feed components that need an interval, such as Range, Remap Numbers or curve evaluation.

commands.name: Deconstruct Domain
commands.description: Splits a domain into its start and end values. Use it to read the extent of a curve's parameter space or the bounds returned by other components.

commands.name: Bounds
commands.description: Finds the smallest domain that encloses a list of numbers, in other words its minimum-to-maximum extent. It is the usual first step before remapping analysis values into a 0–1 range.

commands.name: Remap Numbers
commands.description: Maps numbers from a source domain into a target domain, preserving their relative positions. This is the key component for normalising data — for instance turning distances into 0–1 values that drive colour or geometry.

commands.name: Round
commands.description: Rounds numbers to the nearest whole value, also outputting the floor and ceiling. Use it wherever fractional results must become counts or indices.

commands.name: Average
commands.description: Computes the arithmetic mean of a list of numbers (or the average of points). Handy for finding centres of point clusters or summarising analysis results.

commands.name: Maximum
commands.description: Returns the larger of two values, item by item. Use it to clamp results to a lower limit or to compare alternative measurements.

commands.name: Minimum
commands.description: Returns the smaller of two values, item by item. Combine with Maximum to clamp numbers into a safe range.

commands.name: Pi
commands.description: Outputs the constant pi, optionally multiplied by a factor. Feed it into trigonometry or polar arrays where angles are expressed in radians.

commands.name: Sine
commands.description: Computes the sine of an angle given in radians. A building block for wave-like patterns, facade modulation and circular motion.

commands.name: Cosine
commands.description: Computes the cosine of an angle given in radians. Pair it with Sine to place points on circles or to build periodic rhythms.

commands.name: Tangent
commands.description: Computes the tangent of an angle given in radians. Useful for slope calculations and converting angles to gradients.

commands.name: Radians
commands.description: Converts angles from degrees to radians. Most Grasshopper components expect radians, so this conversion appears constantly next to rotation inputs.

commands.name: Degrees
commands.description: Converts angles from radians to degrees, typically for legible reporting. Use it when displaying angular results in panels or annotations.

commands.name: Series
commands.description: Generates an arithmetic sequence from a start value, step size and count. It is the workhorse for regular spacing — grid setting-out, floor levels and repeated offsets all begin here.

commands.name: Range
commands.description: Divides a domain into an equal number of steps and outputs the resulting values, including both ends. Use it when you need a fixed count of values spanning a known interval, such as parameters along a curve.

commands.name: Random
commands.description: Produces a list of pseudo-random numbers within a domain, controlled by a seed so results are repeatable. Change the seed to explore variations; keep it fixed to lock a design down.

commands.name: Repeat Data
commands.description: Repeats a list until it reaches a target length. Ideal for tiling a short pattern, such as alternating True/False, across a long list of panels.

commands.name: Duplicate Data
commands.description: Copies a list a set number of times, either as whole-list repetitions or with items repeated in place. Useful for matching list lengths before pairwise operations.

commands.name: Cull Pattern
commands.description: Removes items from a list wherever a repeating Boolean pattern reads False. It is the standard way to filter geometry by rule — keep every other panel, drop items that fail a test, and so on.

commands.name: Cull Index
commands.description: Removes items at specific index positions from a list. Use it to delete known outliers, such as the first and last points of a division.

commands.name: Cull Nth
commands.description: Removes every Nth item from a list. A quick way to thin dense point sets or skip repeating structural bays.

commands.name: Jitter
commands.description: Shuffles the order of a list by a controllable amount, from a slight nudge to a full random reshuffle, using a seed for repeatability. Use it to randomise assignment of colours, heights or types across elements.

commands.name: List Item
commands.description: Retrieves the item at a given index from a list, with optional wrapping. Probably the most-used data component: it plucks a specific point, curve or value out of any collection.

commands.name: List Length
commands.description: Reports how many items a list contains. Use it to drive counts elsewhere, or with a Panel as a quick sanity check while debugging data trees.

commands.name: Shift List
commands.description: Offsets the order of a list by a number of steps, with or without wrapping. Shifting a copy of a point list by one against the original is the classic way to draw lines between consecutive points.

commands.name: Reverse List
commands.description: Flips the order of a list end to end. Use it to correct curve direction issues or to pair first items with last ones.

commands.name: Sort List
commands.description: Sorts numeric keys ascending and reorders any synchronised lists along with them. Sort points by height, panels by area, or results by score, then take the extremes with List Item.

commands.name: Insert Items
commands.description: Inserts items into a list at specified indices, pushing later entries along. Use it to splice special elements into an otherwise regular sequence.

commands.name: Replace Items
commands.description: Swaps the items at given indices for new values, leaving the rest of the list untouched. Handy for overriding specific members of a pattern, such as making one facade bay a door.

commands.name: Split List
commands.description: Cuts a list into two at a chosen index, outputting both halves. Use it to separate a leading group from the remainder without losing anything.

commands.name: Sub List
commands.description: Extracts a contiguous slice of a list defined by a domain of indices. Use it to isolate, say, items 10 to 20 from a long sequence.

commands.name: Partition List
commands.description: Chops a flat list into equal-sized chunks, producing a tree with one branch per chunk. It is the quickest way to turn a long point list back into rows for surfacing or panelling.

commands.name: Dispatch
commands.description: Routes list items into two outputs according to a Boolean pattern: True items go one way, False the other. Unlike Cull Pattern it keeps both groups, which makes it ideal for treating two populations differently and recombining later.

commands.name: Weave
commands.description: Merges several lists into one by following a repeating index pattern, interleaving their items. It is the inverse of Dispatch and rebuilds ordered sequences from separated groups.

commands.name: Flatten Tree
commands.description: Collapses a data tree of any depth into a single flat list. Use it when branch structure no longer matters — for example before counting or sorting everything together.

commands.name: Graft Tree
commands.description: Moves every item into its own branch, adding a level to the tree. Grafting changes how lists pair up between components, and is the usual fix when you need one-to-many matching.

commands.name: Simplify Tree
commands.description: Removes redundant path segments that all branches share, shortening paths without changing the data. Simplifying keeps trees legible and helps components with different sources line up.

commands.name: Trim Tree
commands.description: Merges the outermost branches of a tree, reducing its depth by a chosen number of levels. Use it to step back up the hierarchy after operations that grafted data.

commands.name: Flip Matrix
commands.description: Swaps rows and columns in a tree whose branches form a grid, so items grouped by row become grouped by column. Essential for panelling workflows where you need to switch between U-direction and V-direction lists.

commands.name: Path Mapper
commands.description: Rewrites tree paths using a lexical mapping you type, allowing arbitrary restructuring — renumbering, merging or permuting branches. It is the most powerful and least forgiving tree tool, so keep a Panel nearby to check the result.

commands.name: Entwine
commands.description: Combines several inputs into one tree, giving each source its own branch. Use it to bundle related streams — say options A, B and C — so they travel together through the definition.

commands.name: Explode Tree
commands.description: Splits a tree into separate outputs, one per branch, so each can be wired independently. Right-click to match outputs to the current branch count. The canvas nickname is BANG!.

commands.name: Merge
commands.description: Joins multiple data streams into one, appending matching branches in input order. Use it to bring parallel results back together, for instance recombining dispatched groups.

commands.name: Tree Branch
commands.description: Retrieves the list stored at a specific branch path of a tree. It is List Item's counterpart one level up: use it to isolate a single row from a grid of data.

commands.name: Tree Statistics
commands.description: Reports a tree's structure: its paths, the item count per branch and the total branch count. Wire it into panels to understand exactly how data is organised before restructuring it.

commands.name: Clean Tree
commands.description: Strips null items, invalid data and empty branches out of a tree. Run it after intersections or projections that may return misses, so downstream components receive only valid geometry.

commands.name: Concatenate
commands.description: Joins several text fragments into one string in input order. Use it to assemble labels such as panel names built from row and column numbers.

commands.name: Text Join
commands.description: Merges a list of strings into a single string with a separator between entries. Ideal for building comma-separated exports or multi-line schedule text.

commands.name: Text Split
commands.description: Breaks a string into a list wherever separator characters occur. Use it to parse imported data such as CSV lines into individual values.

commands.name: Format
commands.description: Builds a string from a template with numbered placeholders filled by the inputs, including number formatting. Use it for tidy labels like level names with fixed decimal places.

commands.name: Construct Point
commands.description: Creates a point from X, Y and Z coordinate values. It is the fundamental generator of positions, usually fed by sliders or Series components to set out grids.

commands.name: Deconstruct
commands.description: Breaks a point into its X, Y and Z coordinate values. Use it to read positions for sorting, remapping or rebuilding points with one coordinate altered.

commands.name: Distance
commands.description: Measures the straight-line distance between two points. It is the core of attractor patterns: distances to an attractor point are remapped to drive panel openings, heights or colours.

commands.name: Closest Point
commands.description: Finds which point in a cloud lies nearest to a test point, returning the point, its index and the distance. Use it to pair elements with their nearest neighbours or to look up positions in a reference set.

commands.name: Populate 2D
commands.description: Scatters a set number of points quasi-randomly across a rectangular region, with a seed for repeatability and an option to include existing points. A quick way to seed Voronoi diagrams or random planting layouts.

commands.name: Populate 3D
commands.description: Distributes points quasi-randomly through a box volume. Use it for volumetric studies such as 3D Voronoi structures or random spatial arrays.

commands.name: Populate Geometry
commands.description: Scatters points evenly across any geometry — a surface, brep or mesh — rather than a plain rectangle. Ideal for sampling facades or terrain with well-spaced test points.

commands.name: Vector XYZ
commands.description: Builds a vector from X, Y and Z components. Vectors carry direction and magnitude, driving translations, extrusions and orientation throughout Grasshopper.

commands.name: Vector 2Pt
commands.description: Creates the vector pointing from one point to another, with an option to unitise it, and reports its length. Use it to aim geometry at targets or to measure directed offsets.

commands.name: Unit X
commands.description: Outputs a vector along the world X axis with a settable length factor. A convenient shorthand wherever a horizontal direction is needed.

commands.name: Unit Y
commands.description: Outputs a vector along the world Y axis with a settable length factor. Use it for translations and array directions in plan.

commands.name: Unit Z
commands.description: Outputs a vector along the world Z axis with a settable length factor. The default choice for vertical moves and extrusions, such as giving walls height.

commands.name: Amplitude
commands.description: Sets a vector's length to an exact value while keeping its direction. Use it to normalise mixed-length vectors before scaling moves or offsets by data.

commands.name: Unitize
commands.description: Rescales a vector to length one, keeping only its direction. Unit vectors are the safest input for frames, normals and controlled offsets.

commands.name: Vector Length
commands.description: Measures the magnitude of a vector. Combine with Vector 2Pt as an alternative to Distance, or use it to check normals and forces.

commands.name: Cross Product
commands.description: Computes the vector perpendicular to two input vectors. Use it to derive surface normals from edge directions or to build consistent local axes.

commands.name: Dot Product
commands.description: Multiplies two vectors into a single number that reflects how aligned they are. Use it to test whether faces point towards the sun or to sort elements by orientation.

commands.name: Rotate Vector
commands.description: Rotates a vector by an angle (in radians) around an axis. Use it to fan directions around a centre or tilt a direction incrementally.

commands.name: XY Plane
commands.description: Outputs a plane aligned with the world XY axes at a chosen origin. Planes act as local coordinate systems, so this is the default base for rectangles, circles and transforms in plan.

commands.name: XZ Plane
commands.description: Outputs a plane aligned with the world XZ axes at a chosen origin — effectively a front elevation plane. Use it to draw and array geometry vertically.

commands.name: YZ Plane
commands.description: Outputs a plane aligned with the world YZ axes at a chosen origin — a side elevation plane. Useful for sections and lateral setting-out.

commands.name: Construct Plane
commands.description: Builds a plane from an origin point and two axis vectors. Use it when geometry must follow a custom local orientation rather than the world axes.

commands.name: Plane Normal
commands.description: Creates a plane from an origin and a normal (Z) direction, letting Grasshopper choose sensible X and Y axes. The fastest way to make working planes perpendicular to a known direction.

commands.name: Deconstruct Plane
commands.description: Splits a plane into its origin point and X, Y and Z axis vectors. Use it to inspect frames returned by curve or surface evaluation and reuse their parts.

commands.name: Square Grid
commands.description: Generates a grid of square cells with their corner points, given a base plane, cell size and extent counts. A ready-made setting-out grid for panelling, columns or urban studies.

commands.name: Rectangular
commands.description: Generates a grid of rectangular cells with independent X and Y spacing. Use it where structural bays differ in each direction.

commands.name: Hexagonal
commands.description: Generates a honeycomb grid of hexagonal cells and their corner points. Popular for facade patterns, paving studies and cellular structures.

commands.name: Line
commands.description: Creates a straight line between two points. The simplest curve component, used everywhere from structural axes to panel edges.

commands.name: Line SDL
commands.description: Creates a line from a start point, a direction and a length. Use it when you know where a line begins and which way it should go, such as projecting sight lines or setting out mullions.

commands.name: Polyline
commands.description: Connects a list of points into a polyline, optionally closed. Use it to trace boundaries through ordered points, such as building footprints.

commands.name: Circle
commands.description: Creates a circle on a base plane with a given radius. Combine with planes along a curve to make frames for pipes and towers.

commands.name: Circle CNR
commands.description: Creates a circle from a centre point, normal direction and radius. Useful when circles must sit perpendicular to a rail curve or surface normal.

commands.name: Arc
commands.description: Creates an arc on a plane from a radius and an angle domain. Use it for fan shapes, curved setting-out and partial revolutions.

commands.name: Arc 3Pt
commands.description: Creates an arc passing through three points. The natural choice when an arc must hit known positions, such as a vault through survey points.

commands.name: Ellipse
commands.description: Creates an ellipse on a plane from two radii. Use it for oval plans, arches and stadium-like geometries.

commands.name: Rectangle
commands.description: Creates a rectangle on a plane from X and Y size domains, with optional corner fillets. The staple boundary for floor plates, panels and openings.

commands.name: Polygon
commands.description: Creates a regular polygon on a plane from a radius and segment count, with optional fillets. Use it for columns, bolt patterns and faceted plans.

commands.name: Interpolate
commands.description: Draws a smooth curve that passes exactly through a list of points, with control over degree and periodicity. Use it when the curve must hit every point, such as tracing site contours.

commands.name: Nurbs Curve
commands.description: Builds a NURBS curve using the input points as control points, so the curve is guided by them but does not pass through them. It generally produces fairer curves than interpolation and suits freeform design work.

commands.name: Catenary
commands.description: Creates the natural hanging-chain curve between two points for a given length and gravity direction. Architects use it for efficient arch and shell profiles, inverted to work in pure compression.

commands.name: Tween Curve
commands.description: Generates an intermediate curve between two input curves at a chosen blend factor. Use a series of factors to produce graded families of curves, such as roof ribs morphing across a span.

commands.name: Divide Curve
commands.description: Splits a curve into equal-length segments, outputting the division points, tangents and parameters. This is the default way to place repeating elements — columns, mullions, planting — along any curve.

commands.name: Divide Length
commands.description: Places division points along a curve at a fixed length interval measured along the curve, leaving any remainder at the end. Use it when spacing must be exact, such as balustrade posts at set centres.

commands.name: Divide Distance
commands.description: Places points along a curve so that each is a fixed straight-line (chord) distance from the previous one. Useful for panelising curved facades with flat elements of equal width.

commands.name: Perp Frames
commands.description: Distributes planes along a curve that sit perpendicular to it, evenly spaced by count. These frames are the standard scaffolding for sweeping ribs, placing sections or orienting components along a path.

commands.name: Horizontal Frames
commands.description: Distributes planes along a curve that stay horizontal (world XY orientation) while following the curve. Use them where elements must remain level, such as treads along a helical stair.

commands.name: Curve Frames
commands.description: Places a set count of frames along a curve using its own tangent and curvature directions. A general alternative to Perp Frames when the curve's natural orientation is wanted.

commands.name: Shatter
commands.description: Cuts a curve into pieces at a list of parameters, keeping every fragment. Pair it with intersection or closest-point components to break curves exactly where they meet other geometry.

commands.name: Evaluate Curve
commands.description: Returns the point, tangent and angle at a given parameter along a curve. Reparameterise the input so 0–1 maps to the whole curve, then use it to find any fractional position.

commands.name: Curve Closest Point
commands.description: Finds the point on a curve nearest to a test point, returning the point, its parameter and the distance. Use it to snap external points onto a setting-out line or to measure clearances.

commands.name: Length
commands.description: Measures the length of a curve. Feed it into schedules, cost estimates or checks against maximum member lengths.

commands.name: End Points
commands.description: Outputs the start and end points of a curve. Use it to anchor connections, label extents or test whether curves join tip to tip.

commands.name: Control Points
commands.description: Extracts a curve's control points, weights and knots. Use it to rebuild or deform curves by manipulating their control net directly.

commands.name: Curvature
commands.description: Evaluates the curvature vector and centre at a parameter on a curve. Use it to check how tightly a facade curve bends against material bending limits.

commands.name: Offset Curve
commands.description: Creates a parallel copy of a curve at a set distance on a chosen side, with corner style options. The basis of wall thicknesses, path edges and clearance zones.

commands.name: Fillet
commands.description: Rounds the corners of a curve with arcs of a given radius. Use it to soften polyline corners for paths, slabs or extrusion profiles.

commands.name: Join Curves
commands.description: Merges curves whose ends touch into continuous curves. Run it after intersections or explosions to reassemble outlines before surfacing.

commands.name: Explode
commands.description: Breaks a curve into its segments at kinks and knots, outputting the pieces and their vertices. Use it to treat each edge of a rectangle or polyline separately.

commands.name: Rebuild Curve
commands.description: Reconstructs a curve with a chosen degree and control-point count, discarding excess complexity. Use it to fair wobbly imported curves or reduce data before lofting.

commands.name: Flip Curve
commands.description: Reverses a curve's direction, optionally matching it to a guide curve. Consistent direction matters for lofts, offsets and frames, and this is the fix when they misbehave.

commands.name: Extend Curve
commands.description: Lengthens a curve at either end by set distances, with line, arc or smooth extension styles. Use it to guarantee overlaps before trims and intersections.

commands.name: Project
commands.description: Projects curves onto a brep or surface along a direction, like casting a shadow. Use it to map site boundaries onto terrain or drop patterns onto curved facades.

commands.name: Pull Curve
commands.description: Pulls a curve onto a surface by closest points rather than along a fixed direction, so the result hugs the surface. Prefer it over Project when the target wraps or the direction is ambiguous.

commands.name: Extrude
commands.description: Extrudes a curve or surface along a vector, turning profiles into walls and surfaces into solids. With a Unit Z vector it is the quickest route from plan to massing.

commands.name: Loft
commands.description: Skins a surface through an ordered set of section curves, with options for tightness and closed lofts. The classic way to build hulls, towers and roofs from a family of profiles.

commands.name: Sweep1
commands.description: Sweeps one or more section profiles along a single rail curve to form a surface. Use it for handrails, edge beams and any element defined by a profile travelling a path.

commands.name: Sweep2
commands.description: Sweeps sections along two rail curves, giving control over both edges of the resulting surface. Choose it over Sweep1 when the surface must respect two distinct boundaries, like a canopy between two beams.

commands.name: Revolution
commands.description: Revolves a profile curve around an axis to create a surface of revolution. Use it for domes, columns and any rotationally symmetric form; limit the angle domain for partial revolves.

commands.name: Network Surface
commands.description: Builds a surface through a criss-crossing network of curves in two directions. It handles complex freeform patches that Loft cannot, provided the curves intersect cleanly.

commands.name: Boundary Surfaces
commands.description: Creates planar surfaces from closed planar boundary curves, respecting holes when inner loops are supplied. The standard way to turn footprints and floor outlines into surfaces.

commands.name: Patch
commands.description: Fits a surface across a boundary and optional interior points, even where edges are not perfectly coordinated. Use it to close awkward holes or drape a surface over scattered survey data.

commands.name: Surface From Points
commands.description: Builds a surface through a rectangular grid of points, given the count in one direction. Use it to reconstruct terrain or freeform skins from ordered point data.

commands.name: Edge Surface
commands.description: Creates a surface from two, three or four edge curves. A quick, predictable patch when you already have the boundary in place.

commands.name: 4Point Surface
commands.description: Creates a surface spanning three or four corner points. Ideal for quick quads in panelling workflows where corners are already computed.

commands.name: Pipe
commands.description: Wraps a circular-section tube around a rail curve with a set radius and cap options. The fastest way to visualise structural members, handrails and services runs.

commands.name: Center Box
commands.description: Creates a box centred on a plane with X, Y and Z half-dimensions. Useful for massing blocks and bounding volumes symmetrical about a point.

commands.name: Sphere
commands.description: Creates a sphere from a base plane and radius. Use it for markers, domes and boolean tooling shapes.

commands.name: Cylinder
commands.description: Creates a cylinder from a base plane, radius and height. Handy for columns, cores and quick boolean subtractions.

commands.name: Cone
commands.description: Creates a cone from a base plane, radius and height. Use it for roof forms, light cones and transitional geometry.

commands.name: Plane Surface
commands.description: Creates a rectangular surface aligned to a plane with given X and Y size domains. A useful ground plane, cutting tool or panelling base.

commands.name: Evaluate Surface
commands.description: Returns the point, normal and frame at a UV coordinate on a surface. Reparameterise the surface so UV runs 0–1, then use it to place objects anywhere on a skin with correct orientation.

commands.name: Surface Closest Point
commands.description: Finds the nearest point on a surface to a sample point, with its UV coordinates and distance. Use it to project points onto skins or measure how far elements sit from a reference surface.

commands.name: Area
commands.description: Computes the area and centroid of surfaces, breps, meshes or planar closed curves. Essential for schedules of accommodation, facade take-offs and centring geometry.

commands.name: Volume
commands.description: Computes the volume and centroid of closed breps and meshes. Use it for massing studies, cut-and-fill balances and material quantities.

commands.name: Deconstruct Brep
commands.description: Breaks a brep into its faces, edges and vertices as separate lists. The gateway to working with individual faces of a massing model or the edge curves of a panel.

commands.name: Offset Surface
commands.description: Creates a copy of a surface offset along its normals by a distance, optionally retrimmed. Use it to give skins depth, such as generating the inner face of a shell.

commands.name: Isotrim
commands.description: Extracts the rectangular portion of a surface defined by a UV domain. Combined with Divide Domain², it is the core of panelling: the skin is chopped into a grid of sub-surfaces.

commands.name: Divide Domain²
commands.description: Splits a surface's two-dimensional UV domain into a grid of U by V segments. Feed the resulting domains into Isotrim to panelise any surface.

commands.name: Divide Surface
commands.description: Generates a grid of points, normals and UV coordinates across a surface at set U and V counts. Use it to set out facade nodes or sample a skin for analysis.

commands.name: Cap Holes
commands.description: Fills planar openings in a brep to make it closed. Run it after extrusions or booleans that leave open ends, since many volume and boolean operations require watertight solids.

commands.name: Brep Join
commands.description: Joins adjacent breps and surfaces that share edges into fewer, larger breps. Use it to assemble faces back into a solid after editing them individually.

commands.name: Solid Union
commands.description: Merges overlapping closed breps into a single solid, dissolving internal faces. Use it to fuse massing blocks before area, volume or facade operations.

commands.name: Solid Difference
commands.description: Subtracts one set of closed breps from another, cutting holes and voids. The standard way to punch window openings or carve courtyards from a massing.

commands.name: Solid Intersection
commands.description: Keeps only the volume shared by two sets of closed breps. Use it to clip masses to zoning envelopes or find overlapping volumes between disciplines.

commands.name: Split Brep
commands.description: Splits a brep with a cutting brep or surface, keeping every resulting piece. Unlike a boolean it discards nothing, so you choose which fragments to keep afterwards with List Item or Cull.

commands.name: Trim Solid
commands.description: Removes the parts of a solid that fall inside (or outside) a trimming solid. A directional alternative to Split Brep when you know which side to discard.

commands.name: Brep | Brep
commands.description: Computes the intersection curves and points where two breps meet. Use it to find junction lines between walls and roofs or clash lines between elements.

commands.name: Brep | Plane
commands.description: Intersects a brep with a plane, returning the section curves. Drive the plane's elevation with a slider and you have a live building section; repeat with Series for floor plans at every level.

commands.name: Curve | Curve
commands.description: Finds the intersection points between two curves, with the parameters on each. Combine with Shatter to cut curves precisely where they cross, as in grid and beam layouts.

commands.name: Contour
commands.description: Slices a brep or mesh with a series of parallel planes at a set spacing, returning the contour curves. The go-to component for site contours, sectional models and waffle structures.

commands.name: Region Union
commands.description: Merges overlapping closed planar curves into combined outlines. Use it to fuse adjoining footprints or paving regions into a single boundary.

commands.name: Region Difference
commands.description: Subtracts closed planar curves from others within a plane, producing trimmed outlines. Ideal for cutting openings out of floor-plate boundaries before surfacing.

commands.name: Mesh Brep
commands.description: Converts brep geometry into meshes using quality settings you control. Meshing is a prerequisite for many analysis, rendering and fabrication tools, and for all Weaverbird-style modelling.

commands.name: Construct Mesh
commands.description: Builds a mesh from a list of vertices and face definitions, with optional colours. Use it for full control of topology, for example when generating panels or importing data point-by-point.

commands.name: Deconstruct Mesh
commands.description: Splits a mesh into its vertices, faces, colours and normals. The starting point for per-vertex analysis, recolouring and topology edits.

commands.name: Mesh Join
commands.description: Combines multiple meshes into one mesh object. Join panels before welding or export so downstream tools treat them as a single body.

commands.name: Weld Mesh
commands.description: Merges coincident mesh vertices whose normals differ by less than a threshold angle, smoothing shading across seams. Weld after joining so a panelised mesh reads as a continuous skin.

commands.name: Smooth Mesh
commands.description: Relaxes mesh vertices towards the average of their neighbours over several iterations, softening the form. Use it to ease noisy scan data or organically round a faceted model.

commands.name: Triangulate
commands.description: Converts the quads in a mesh into triangles. Triangulated meshes are required by many structural and fabrication workflows because triangles are always planar.

commands.name: Quad Remesh
commands.description: Rebuilds any mesh or brep as a clean, quad-dominant mesh with controllable density and edge-flow guides. Use it to prepare geometry for subdivision modelling, simulation or SubD conversion.

commands.name: Delaunay Mesh
commands.description: Creates a triangulated mesh across a set of points using Delaunay logic, which avoids skinny triangles. The standard route from survey points to a terrain mesh.

commands.name: Voronoi
commands.description: Generates the Voronoi diagram of a point set: planar cells where each cell contains the region closest to one point. A favourite generator for organic facade patterns, paving and spatial partitions.

commands.name: Voronoi 3D
commands.description: Computes volumetric Voronoi cells around points within a box, outputting closed cell breps. Use it for porous massing studies and cellular structural concepts.

commands.name: Convex Hull
commands.description: Finds the smallest convex polyline enclosing a set of points in a plane. Use it for site extents, bounding footprints and quick massing envelopes around scattered data.

commands.name: Face Normals
commands.description: Evaluates the centre point and normal vector of every mesh face. Use the normals for orientation-based analysis such as sun exposure, or to place components on each face.

commands.name: Move
commands.description: Translates geometry along a vector, outputting the moved geometry and the transform. Pair it with unit vectors and Series to copy elements at regular spacings.

commands.name: Rotate
commands.description: Rotates geometry by an angle (in radians) within a plane. Combine with Radians and a slider for interactive rotation about any working plane.

commands.name: Rotate Axis
commands.description: Rotates geometry around an arbitrary axis line by a given angle. Use it for tilting panels about their edges or opening rooflights about a hinge.

commands.name: Scale
commands.description: Scales geometry uniformly about a centre point by a factor. Use graded factors along a list to taper repeated elements.

commands.name: Scale NU
commands.description: Scales geometry non-uniformly with independent factors along a plane's X, Y and Z axes. Ideal for stretching a prototype panel to fit varying bay widths.

commands.name: Mirror
commands.description: Reflects geometry across a plane. Use it for symmetrical plans and handed pairs of components.

commands.name: Orient
commands.description: Remaps geometry from a source plane to a target plane in one step, combining move and rotation. The cleanest way to place a detailed component onto many frames along a curve or surface.

commands.name: Linear Array
commands.description: Copies geometry a set number of times along a direction vector. The quickest repeat tool for fencing, mullions and bays at even spacing.

commands.name: Polar Array
commands.description: Copies geometry around a centre plane through a total sweep angle. Use it for radial structures, stair balusters on a curve and rotational patterns.

commands.name: Rectangular Array
commands.description: Copies geometry across a two-directional grid defined by a cell and counts. Use it for column grids, ceiling layouts and repeated room modules.

commands.name: Box Array
commands.description: Copies geometry through a three-dimensional grid of cells. Use it to stack modules in X, Y and Z at once, such as prefabricated units in a block.

commands.name: Curve Array
commands.description: Distributes copies of geometry along a curve. Use it to run repeating elements along a winding path where a linear array will not follow.

commands.name: Flow
commands.description: Bends geometry from a base curve onto a target curve, stretching it along the new path. Use it to wrap a straight railing detail onto a curved edge.

commands.name: Box Morph
commands.description: Deforms geometry from a reference box into a target twisted box. Combined with Surface Box it populates freeform skins with adapted three-dimensional components — the backbone of many facade systems.

commands.name: Surface Morph
commands.description: Maps geometry from a reference box onto a surface domain with a height range, draping objects across the skin. Use it to spread ribs, patterns or components over doubly curved surfaces.

commands.name: Map to Surface
commands.description: Transfers curves drawn in a flat reference region onto a target surface's UV space. Ideal for laying out a 2D pattern and letting the surface carry it into 3D.

commands.name: Twist
commands.description: Twists geometry around an axis line by an angle, with optional infinite extents. The classic tower-massing move: a straight extrusion becomes a twisting form in one component.

commands.name: Custom Preview
commands.description: Overrides the default red/green preview with a chosen colour or material for the wired geometry. Combine it with Gradient to paint analysis results directly onto the model.

commands.name: Text Tag
commands.description: Draws small screen-aligned text labels at points in the viewport, purely as a preview. Use it to tag indices or values on geometry while debugging a definition.

commands.name: Text Tag 3D
commands.description: Places true 3D text of a set size and orientation at given locations, and it bakes to Rhino text. Use it to label panels, levels or grid lines in a way that survives baking.

commands.name: Aligned Dimension
commands.description: Previews a linear dimension between two points on a plane, with offset and text options, and bakes as a real Rhino dimension. Use it to annotate parametric drawings straight from the definition.

commands.name: Solver
commands.description: The physics engine at the heart of Kangaroo: it takes a list of goal objects and iteratively moves particles until the goals reach equilibrium. Use it for form-finding, relaxation and constraint solving, with a reset input to restart the simulation.

commands.name: Anchor
commands.description: A goal that pins chosen points in place (or pulls them towards targets) during a Kangaroo simulation. Anchors define the supports of a form-found structure, such as the corners of a hanging membrane.

commands.name: Length (Line)
commands.description: A goal that makes line segments try to reach a target length with a given strength, behaving like springs. Networks of these springs relax gridshells and cable nets into efficient shapes.

commands.name: Load
commands.description: A goal that applies a force vector, such as gravity, to points in the simulation. Combine loads with springs and anchors to hang chains and drape membranes that invert into compression forms.

commands.name: SphereCollide
commands.description: A goal that keeps a set of points at least a sphere-diameter apart, resolving collisions between many objects efficiently. Use it for circle packing and evenly distributing elements across surfaces.

commands.name: OnMesh
commands.description: A goal that constrains points to remain on a target mesh while other goals act on them. Use it to relax patterns or pack circles across a doubly curved skin without leaving the surface.

commands.name: LB Import EPW
commands.description: Reads an EnergyPlus weather file (EPW) and outputs its climate data streams: temperatures, radiation, wind, humidity and more. Every Ladybug study starts here, so the location's real climate drives the analysis.

commands.name: LB SunPath
commands.description: Draws an interactive sun-path diagram for a location and reports sun position vectors for chosen dates and times. Use the vectors to test shadows, orient massing or drive shading design.

commands.name: LB Incident Radiation
commands.description: Calculates the solar radiation falling on test geometry over a period, using a cumulative sky from the weather file, and colours the mesh with the results. Use it to compare facade options or locate photovoltaic potential.

commands.name: LB Direct Sun Hours
commands.description: Counts the hours of direct sunlight received by geometry for given sun vectors, accounting for surrounding context as obstructions. A staple for rights-of-light studies and outdoor comfort checks.

commands.name: LB Wind Rose
commands.description: Plots a wind rose from hourly weather data, showing the frequency, direction and speed of winds at the site. Use it to inform natural ventilation strategy and outdoor space placement.

commands.name: HB Room from Solid
commands.description: Converts closed solid volumes into Honeybee rooms — the zoned building blocks of energy and daylight models — deriving faces, boundary conditions and adjacencies. It is the bridge from massing model to simulation model.

commands.name: HB Aperture
commands.description: Creates window apertures from surfaces and assigns them to room faces. Apertures carry glazing properties, so they control daylight and solar gains in downstream simulations.

commands.name: HB Model
commands.description: Assembles rooms, apertures, shades and context into a single Honeybee model object ready for simulation. All Honeybee recipes consume a model, making this the final packaging step before analysis.

commands.name: HB Annual Daylight
commands.description: Runs an annual daylight simulation with Radiance over a Honeybee model, returning metrics such as daylight autonomy for each sensor grid. Use it to evidence daylight standards and compare design options.

commands.name: Line to Beam
commands.description: Converts line geometry into Karamba beam elements, with identifiers for later property assignment. It is the first step in turning a wireframe structural concept into an analysable model.

commands.name: Support
commands.description: Defines support conditions at points, fixing or releasing each translation and rotation. Supports anchor the structural model, and their conditions strongly shape the resulting forces.

commands.name: Loads
commands.description: Creates structural loads — gravity, point, line or mesh loads — for the model. Combine several load types into cases to test how the structure responds.

commands.name: Assemble Model
commands.description: Gathers elements, supports, loads, materials and cross-sections into a complete Karamba structural model. The assembled model is the single object passed on to the analysis components.

commands.name: Analyze
commands.description: Runs a linear elastic analysis on an assembled model, computing displacements, forces and utilisation. Its outputs feed result viewers and optimisation loops, closing the design-analysis cycle inside Grasshopper.

commands.name: Model View
commands.description: Displays an analysed Karamba model with deformation, force diagrams and utilisation colouring in the viewport. Use it to read results visually and communicate structural behaviour to the design team.

commands.name: Quad Panels
commands.description: Divides a surface into a U by V grid of quadrilateral panels in one step. A fast route to rational facade grids without building the Isotrim workflow by hand.

commands.name: Diamond Panels
commands.description: Panelises a surface with a diagonal grid of diamond-shaped panels. Use it for diagrid facades and lattice shells where members run at forty-five degrees to the surface directions.

commands.name: Triangle Panels A
commands.description: Divides a surface into triangular panels in one of LunchBox's triangulation arrangements. Triangular panels guarantee planarity, which simplifies glazing and cladding fabrication.

commands.name: Hexagon Cells
commands.description: Maps a honeycomb of hexagonal cells across a surface. Use it for cellular facades and screens; note that hexagons on curved surfaces are generally non-planar and need further rationalisation.

commands.name: Tween Two Curves
commands.description: Generates any number of intermediate curves between two boundary curves, with matching and interpolation options beyond the native tween. Use it for graded rib systems and smooth transitions between profiles.

commands.name: Tween Two Surfaces
commands.description: Creates intermediate surfaces blending between two input surfaces. Use it to morph a roof between two design states or generate layered shell studies.

commands.name: Tween Consecutive Curves
commands.description: Tweens through a whole list of curves in order, inserting intermediate curves between each consecutive pair. Ideal for densifying a sparse set of sections before lofting.

commands.name: Catmull-Clark Subdivision
commands.description: Subdivides a mesh using the Catmull-Clark scheme, rounding the form towards a smooth limit surface with each iteration. The classic way to turn a coarse box-modelled mass into a refined organic shape.

commands.name: Loop Subdivision
commands.description: Subdivides triangular meshes with the Loop scheme, smoothing while keeping an all-triangle topology. Prefer it over Catmull-Clark when downstream tools expect triangles.

commands.name: Mesh Thicken
commands.description: Gives a mesh solid thickness by offsetting it and stitching the edges closed. Use it to turn panelised skins and lattices into printable, buildable solids.

commands.name: Picture Frame
commands.description: Replaces each mesh face with a frame by insetting a hole into it, keeping the border. Applied before thickening, it converts any mesh into a cellular lattice or gridshell-like screen.

commands.name: Bake Objects
commands.description: Bakes geometry into the Rhino document with full control of layer, name, colour and user attributes, replacing earlier bakes of the same objects. It turns Grasshopper into a documentation pipeline, keeping the Rhino file organised automatically.

commands.name: Define Object Attributes
commands.description: Builds an attribute set — layer, object name, colour and user text key-values — to accompany geometry when baking. Attach data such as panel IDs so downstream schedules and fabrication files stay linked to geometry.

commands.name: Reference by Layer
commands.description: References Rhino geometry onto the canvas by layer name, keeping the link live as the layer's contents change. With baking components it enables round-trip workflows between the model and the definition.

commands.name: Custom Preview Materials
commands.description: Previews geometry with render materials including transparency, shine and textures, going well beyond the flat colours of the native preview. Use it for presentation-quality viewport captures straight from the definition.

commands.name: Create/Modify Layers
commands.description: Creates Rhino layers, including nested hierarchies, and sets their colours and states from Grasshopper. Use it to build a project layer structure automatically before baking geometry into it.

commands.name: Galapagos
commands.description: An evolutionary solver that repeatedly adjusts chosen sliders to minimise or maximise a single fitness value. Use it to search for optima a human would struggle to find, such as the panel layout with least material waste.

commands.name: Octopus
commands.description: A multi-objective evolutionary solver that explores trade-offs between several fitness values at once, presenting the Pareto front of best compromises. Use it when goals conflict, such as maximising daylight while minimising solar gain.

commands.name: Wallacei X
commands.description: A multi-objective evolutionary engine with rich analytics for exploring the results: clustering, parallel-coordinate plots and generation-by-generation selection. Use it for rigorous design-space exploration where understanding the population matters as much as the single best answer.

commands.name: Nest
commands.description: Arranges flat closed curves efficiently onto stock sheets of given sizes, rotating and packing parts to minimise waste. The essential step between unrolled panels and CNC cutting files.
